slides.title: What is Type Casting?
slides.content: Type casting converts a variable from one type to another. C# supports implicit casting (safe, automatic) and explicit casting (requires syntax, may lose data).
slides.exampleOutput: Declaration or expression only; produces no console output.

slides.title: Implicit Casting
slides.content: Implicit casting happens automatically when converting from a smaller type to a larger type with no risk of data loss. Examples include int to long, float to double, and char to int.
slides.exampleOutput: Declaration or expression only; produces no console output.

exercise.prompt: What operator or syntax is used for explicit casting?

slides.title: Explicit Casting
slides.content: Use explicit casting with parentheses when converting from a larger type to a smaller one. The compiler requires you to acknowledge possible data loss.
slides.exampleOutput: Declaration or expression only; produces no console output.

exercise.prompt: Complete the explicit cast from double to int.

slides.title: The Convert Class
slides.content: System.Convert provides methods for converting between base types. It handles null strings safely and throws exceptions for invalid formats.
slides.exampleOutput: Declaration or expression only; produces no console output.

exercise.prompt: What does Convert.ToInt32 return when given a null string?

slides.title: Parse Method
slides.content: Parse methods like int.Parse and double.Parse convert strings to numeric types. They throw FormatException if the string is not in a valid format.
slides.exampleOutput: Declaration or expression only; produces no console output.

exercise.prompt: What exception does int.Parse throw on invalid input?

slides.title: TryParse for Safe Conversion
slides.content: TryParse attempts to convert a string and returns true or false instead of throwing exceptions. It is the preferred method when input may be invalid.

slides.title: Common Casting Errors
slides.content: InvalidCastException occurs when an invalid cast is attempted. FormatException occurs when Parse receives malformed input. Always validate input or use TryParse.
slides.exampleOutput: Declaration or expression only; produces no console output.

exercise.prompt: Which method avoids exceptions on invalid string input?

slides.title: Practice: Type Casting
slides.content: Practice converting between types using explicit casting, Convert class methods, and Parse. Combine these with user input for real-world scenarios.

exercise.prompt: Parse a string "45.67" to a double, cast it to an int, and print the int value.
hints: Make sure your code includes the required keywords/elements: Parse, Cast
When run, your code should output: 45
